dct_description_sm: Yukon Government's (YG) climate change adaptation efforts began formally in 2009 with the Yukon Government Climate Change Action Plan and a clear articulation of adaptation as a key government priority. With the addition of Aboriginal Affairs and Northern Development Canada (AANDC), Northern Strategy Trust Fund, and other partnerships, YG was able to mobilize key adaptation projects across the territory. The overall intent was that effective climate change adaptation projects become mainstream activity for YG departments and the communities they affect thereby offering effective climate change adaptation approaches to all Yukoners. The Yukon Government chose several of Yukon's best proposals for adaptation projects and put them forth when applying for AANDC funding. This particular project addressed the fact that many Yukon communities were vulnerable to flooding, and that there was a certain amount of uncertainty around what the exact changes to river flows and water levels would be as Yukon's climate continued to change. Since Yukon had no elevation data for communities bordering rivers and lakes that could provide the detail needed to model areas vulnerable to higher water levels, this project aimed to acquire digital elevation data in the 15 to 20cm range in order to enable detailed modeling that could assist in determining current and future vulnerable areas in and around communities thereby assisting in future flood preparedness and land use planning, and flood mitigation investments all to enhance the community's resiliency.
